craft_notes: Sthāyin: maṅgala-vīra of fear dropped; vyabhicāri ullāsa at mirrored fearlessness; FIRST VERSE — sets the house voice (finishing-rite amid sorrow, sweet-turn, mirrored-mind; owner verdict required). Sanskrit-first: samāpti-kriyā (FINISHING-RITE — kept; the rite completes); duḥkha-gaṇa (SORROW'S-CROWD — kept crowd, not sea); bhaya-tyāga (FEAR-DROPPED — kept dropped). Rows: 1 (‘drops fear’ closes — the rite's effect last), 9 (sorrow-crowd/foul-day pair — the unfit turned sweet), 10 (mirror left standing). Close: ‘the mind drops fear’. Rupture: semicolon (rite stated, then its turning). Rejected: smoothing long-compound — killed by UNC (held as printed); ‘turns→goes’ — killed: turns transforms; ‘reflecting’ for mirrored — killed: mirror mirrors. Read aloud: a-MID sor-row's-CROWD, the FIN-ish-ing-RITE — BLISS-ess-ence SPREAD-ing … the-FOUL-day TURNS-sweet: MIR-rored IN the-HYMN, the-MIND drops-FEAR.

lines: Amid sorrow's crowd, the finishing rite — bliss-essence spreading;
the foul day turns sweet: mirrored in the hymn, the mind drops fear.
l4.sanskrit_cite: duḥkhavrātavrataparigame pāraṇavidhir | mahāsaukhyāsāraprasaraṇarase durdinam idam | pratiphalati ceto gatabhayam

reads_against.argmap: What rite ends sorrow? → The hymn mirrors back the fearful mind into fearlessness.
c1_essence: Completion-rite amid sorrow; mirrored mind drops fear.
